source.title: Stability vs Implicit Bias of Gradient Methods on Separable Data and Beyond

record.file_problem: none; the supplied text contains the full paper and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes stability and generalization bounds for gradient methods on separable linear classification. It does not test the claim versions about random-label memorization, width, architecture, adaptive optimizers, batch size, dropout, sharpness, or removing memorized examples.
record.gate_note: The paper reports theoretical bounds for test loss and test accuracy on separable data. These bear on the broader subject of gradient-method generalization but do not test any listed version. Prior-work results mentioned in the text are not recorded as this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study proves stability and population-loss bounds for convex optimization and separable linear classification. None of its results tests the neural-network comparisons or interventions specified in V1–V8. Its citations to implicit-regularization research do not constitute tests of those versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors derive stability and generalization-loss bounds under realizability and self-boundedness, with applications to separable linear classification. They argue that stability gives tighter guarantees earlier in optimization than available implicit-bias analyses in some settings. These are theoretical guarantees, not empirical demonstrations of V1–V8.
record.recipe_differences: The paper provides theoretical analysis and bounds for unregularized gradient descent and stochastic gradient descent on convex objectives, including separable linear classification; it does not run the empirical recipes in the listed claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The derived bounds depend on loss-tail behavior, margin γ, sample size n, step count T, and the self-boundedness parameters.

fits_no_version.finding: Finite-time expected population-loss upper bounds for separable linear classification depend on loss tails, margin, sample size, and optimization steps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under population separability and the stated regularity conditions, gradient methods admit finite-time population-loss guarantees whose rates depend on the loss function.

fits_no_version.finding: Gradient descent with exponential loss admits an on-average leave-one-out model-stability upper bound.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: On separable bounded data, exponential-loss gradient descent initialized at zero with step size one has leave-one-out model stability O(log²(T)/(γ²n)).

record.problems: The evidence consists of theoretical bounds under stated assumptions rather than empirical measurements. The main general framework assumes nonnegative, convex, smooth losses and realizability/self-boundedness conditions; the paper notes that the probit-loss properties are checked numerically on part of the range.
record.rows_left_out: No otherwise eligible reported theoretical bound was omitted.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label versus random-label held-out performance in the same neural architectures and recipes.
Width-dependent training and test error beyond the width required for interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers, local connectivity, and transferred initialization.
Adaptive versus nonadaptive optimizers and the effects of tuning, weight decay, or optimizer switching.
Batch-size effects under matched epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects, training-set size, excessive dropout, and removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps across similarly fitted convolutional networks.
Accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict labels apply. A worsening upper bound does not itself demonstrate worsening test performance. Comparing GD and SGD bounds here also does not test V5's fixed-epoch batch-size claim.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fit and held-out performance on natural labels are not compared.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.
No sharpness or other measured-property comparison across networks.

rows.operation_detail: Theoretical stability bound for gradient descent on separable data with exponential loss.
rows.measure: ℓ1 on-average leave-one-out model stability ε(1)stab
rows.note: This is a stability bound, not a measured training-to-test gap.
rows.check: The value matches Corollary 39. Leave-one-out model stability measures changes in model parameters, not magnitude-aware sharpness or the removal of highly memorized examples. The appendix explicitly does not establish an exponential-loss generalization guarantee from this stability bound.
